9a

Initially, the only two forces that act on the sphere is the weight downwards and the buoyancy force upwards and since the weight is larger than the buoyancy force, the sphere accelerates downwards.

As the speed of the sphere increases the viscous drag force (pointing upwards) on the sphere increases, so the acceleration of the sphere decreases. 

Around the net force on the sphere drops to zero (from this moment on the weight is equal to the sum of the buoyancy force and the viscous drag force), so afterwards the sphere falls at constant speed.
